vocab.example: Let me give you a scenario: a client is angry about a delay.
vocab.example_vi: Để tôi đưa ra một tình huống: khách hàng tức giận vì bị chậm trễ.

vocab.example: If I had two urgent tasks, I would prioritize the one that affects customers.
vocab.example_vi: Nếu có hai việc gấp, tôi sẽ ưu tiên việc ảnh hưởng đến khách hàng.

vocab.example: Before making a decision, I would gather information from the team.
vocab.example_vi: Trước khi quyết định, tôi sẽ thu thập thông tin từ nhóm.

vocab.example: This kind of question tests your judgment under pressure.
vocab.example_vi: Loại câu hỏi này kiểm tra khả năng phán đoán của bạn khi bị áp lực.

vocab.example: In that case, I would ask my team lead for advice.
vocab.example_vi: Trong trường hợp đó, tôi sẽ xin ý kiến trưởng nhóm.

vocab.example: Working with live customers taught me to think on my feet.
vocab.example_vi: Làm việc trực tiếp với khách hàng đã dạy tôi cách ứng biến nhanh.

vocab.example: I would weigh up the risks before choosing an option.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi sẽ cân nhắc các rủi ro trước khi chọn phương án.

vocab.example: We found a workaround so customers could still pay while we fixed the bug.
vocab.example_vi: Chúng tôi tìm ra giải pháp tạm để khách vẫn thanh toán được trong lúc sửa lỗi.

lines.speaker: Mai (HR Manager)
lines.text: Let me give you a scenario. The release is tomorrow, but you find a serious bug tonight. What would you do?

lines.speaker: Khang (Candidate)
lines.text: First, I would stay focused and gather information. I need to know how serious the bug is.

lines.speaker: Mai (HR Manager)
lines.text: Okay. Let's say it affects the payment page.

lines.speaker: Khang (Candidate)
lines.text: In that case, I would inform my team lead and the product owner right away.

lines.speaker: Mai (HR Manager)
lines.text: Would you try to fix it yourself overnight?

lines.speaker: Khang (Candidate)
lines.text: I would look for a quick workaround first. Then I'd weigh up the options: delay the release, or release without the payment change.

lines.speaker: Mai (HR Manager)
lines.text: And who makes the final decision?

lines.speaker: Khang (Candidate)
lines.text: The product owner should decide. My job is to give clear facts so they can use good judgment.

lines.speaker: Mai (HR Manager)
lines.text: That's a thoughtful answer. You seem able to think on your feet.

lines.speaker: Khang (Candidate)
lines.text: Thank you. Last year we delayed a release by one day, and customers were happy because nothing broke.

questions.q: What does Khang do first in the scenario?
What would Khang look for before deciding?
Who should make the final decision, according to Khang?

shadowing: First, I would gather all the information before making any decision.
In that case, I would inform my manager and the client as soon as possible.
I would prioritize the task that has the biggest impact on our customers.
I would explain the trade-off clearly so my manager could make a good decision.
Last year a similar thing happened, and we delayed the release by one day.
